title: A Spectral-Case-Based Depth Retrieval (SCBDR) Method for Intercontinental-Scale Nearshore Waters: An Application in the Mediterranean Sea
content: Nearshore depths are of great importance for coastal zone management, marine ecological research, and global seafloor mapping, but significant data gaps still exist in nearshore waters due to the high cost and limited spatial coverage of traditional shipborne and airborne methods. Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) can efficiently obtain large-area shallow-water depth information; yet, its retrieval accuracy is affected by spatial variations in water optical properties and seabed substrates. Spectral-regression-based SDB typically relies on regional in situ measurements to calibrate the empirical spectral-depth relationships, which limits its intercontinental-scale applicability. To address this issue, this study proposes a large-scale spectral-case-based depth retrieval (SCBDR) framework, termed SCBDR. The framework integrates spaceborne bathymetric data from the Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2), airborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) bathymetry data, and annual composite Sentinel-2 imagery to construct a spectral-depth case database covering multiple seas and diverse optical environments. During retrieval in a study area, representative case sets are first selected from the dataset based on environmental similarity derived from image spectral features, then spectral band importance is adaptively evaluated and effective bands are selected, and finally, a depth retrieval model suitable for the study area is established. This method does not require separate empirical model calibration for each study area and can dynamically match appropriate spectral-depth relationships according to local environmental characteristics. The proposed approach is validated along the Mediterranean coast, where spatially continuous bathymetry is generated at 10-m resolution for pixels classified as optically shallow water (OSW). Comparison with the resampled EMODnet bathymetric surface yields an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.49 m and root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.69 m. SCBDR maintains the stable performance across different Mediterranean countries, with retrieval accuracy slightly superior to ICESat-2 measured depths and spectral-regression-based bathymetry results and markedly better than global elevation models. The results provide high-resolution and spatially continuous shallow-water depth data for the Mediterranean and offer a reproducible technical framework for large-scale shallow-water bathymetric mapping in data-scarce regions.
author: Guoping Zhang, Shuai Xing, Ruiyao Kong, Li Chen, Pengcheng Li, Dandi Wang, Ming Gao, Jikun Liu, Xinlei Zhang

title: Edge-Guided Adjacent Scale Fusion Network for Building Change Detection With VHR Remote Sensing Images
content: Building change detection (BCD) with very high-resolution (VHR) remotely sensed images (RSIs) is crucial in various remote sensing applications. However, most existing multiscale methods mainly aggregate features from different levels, while the relationships and discriminative differences between adjacent-scale features are seldom explicitly modeled. Existing edge-guided methods generally use building boundaries only as auxiliary constraints, without explicitly exploiting building-edge differences between bitemporal images. In this work, motivated by the idea of utilizing multiscale feature difference, a novel encoder–decoder network called edge-guided adjacent-scale fusion (EGASF) network is proposed for BCD with VHR RSIs. First, taking into account the connection of a target between different scales, an adjacent-scale feature fusion (ASFF) module is constructed to join the features from different scales. Second, a multiscale feature difference metric (MFDM) module is proposed to measure the change magnitude between the learned features of different scales. Finally, a building-edge difference extraction (BEDE) module is proposed and coupled with the learned multiscale difference feature to guide the decoding progress for the task of BCD, complementing the loss of information at the stage of the encoder. Experiments on four pairs of real BCD datasets effectively verified the superiority of the proposed EGASF network compared with eight state-of-the-art methods. Compared with the best-performing competing method on each dataset, the proposed EGASF achieves absolute OA improvements of 0.30, 0.82, and 0.52 percentage points on Data-A, Data-B, and Data-C, respectively, while obtaining a comparable result on Data-D. The code for the proposed EGASF network can be available at https://github.com/ImgSciGroup/EGASF-Net
author: Linfu Xie, Zhiyong Lv, Cheng Shi, Jón Atli Benediktsson, Ziqing Zhao, Lubin Tian

title: Open-Set Cross-Scene Hyperspectral Image Classification With Collaborative Feature and Classifier Adaptation Networks
content: Open-set hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) aims to accurately recognize known categories while rejecting unseen ones. However, existing methods typically assume that training and testing data follow the same distribution. Such an assumption is often violated in cross-scene applications with significant distribution shifts. In this article, we address a more practical and challenging task, termed open-set cross-scene HSIC, which requires simultaneous adaptation to scene distribution discrepancies and reliable detection of unknown categories. To this end, we propose a collaborative feature and classifier adaptation network (CF-CAN) that jointly enhances representation robustness and decision reliability under open-set cross-scene conditions. In particular, an adaptive multiscale feature fusion (AMFF) module is introduced to learn robust and transferable representations, while a class-adaptive dynamic thresholding (CADT) strategy estimates categorywise rejection boundaries for more reliable unknown detection. What’s more, a self-supervised information mining (SSIM) module exploits high-confidence target-domain samples to facilitate domain alignment, improving the separability between known and unknown categories. By collaboratively optimizing feature extraction and classifier adaptation within a unified framework, CF-CAN improves both cross-scene generalization and open-set discrimination. Extensive experiments on three tasks demonstrate that CF-CAN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art HSIC methods.
author: Wuli Wang, Yun Liu, Jianbu Wang, Shuyan Zhang, Sichao Fu, Weihua Ou, Peng Ren

title: GPS-CLIP: GMM-Based Pseudo-Label Refinement for Semi-Supervised Zero-Shot Remote Sensing Classification
content: Remote sensing scene classification (RSSC) plays a crucial role in applications, such as environmental monitoring, urban planning, and disaster management. However, traditional methods often require large amounts of labeled data, which can be both costly and time-consuming to obtain, especially for rare or unseen categories. Zero-shot RSSC (ZSRSSC) aims to overcome this challenge by recognizing categories that were not present in the training set, leveraging external semantic information. Recent advances in vision–language models (VLMs), such as contrastive language–image pretraining (CLIP), have made it possible to align image features with textual descriptions to tackle this problem. We introduce GPS-CLIP, a novel Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based framework that leverages Pseudo-label refinement for Semi-supervised learning with CLIP, enabling effective adaptation to the target domain without any labeled target-domain samples. Under an inductive protocol, adaptation uses only the training split; the frozen model is evaluated on a disjoint test split that never participates in adaptation. GPS-CLIP first generates initial pseudo-labels using a pretrained CLIP model, which are then refined through a GMM that captures feature distribution and label structure. Contrastive fine-tuning progressively adapts the model using balanced, high-confidence samples. By integrating these modules into a unified pipeline, GPS-CLIP improves pseudo-label reliability and visual-semantic alignment. Across five benchmarks and three backbones, GPS-CLIP delivers superior or competitive performance under inductive evaluation.
author: Yang Liu, Suisui Jia, Weixing Luo, Xinbo Gao, Lei Zhang, Ling Shao

title: SSAN: Structured Spatial Aggregation Network With Sparse Partition Routing for Cross-View Geo-Localization
content: Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) aims to retrieve images depicting the same geographic target across heterogeneous viewpoints. Drone–satellite matching remains challenging because holistic descriptors may dilute localized geographic cues, predefined partitions are sensitive to viewpoint- and altitude-induced spatial variations, and exhaustive cross-view interaction may introduce unreliable associations between spatially misaligned regions. To address these issues, we propose a structured spatial aggregation network (SSAN), which couples response-driven regional aggregation with training-time sparse structural regularization. In particular, the soft partitioning module (SPM) learns continuous partition-response maps directly from retrieval supervision and aggregates reduced visual features into structured regional descriptors. Area-aware normalization (AAN) further compensates for differences in partition-response area, attenuating excessive dependence of regional descriptor magnitudes on response extent. Based on the learned response layouts, sparse partition routing (SPR) constructs compact regional tokens, estimates bidirectional cross-view affinities, and retains Top- $r$  high-affinity associations for structural refinement. SPR is applied only during training as a structural regularizer, preserving independent query–gallery encoding at retrieval. Extensive experiments on University-1652, SUES-200, and multiweather University-1652 demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of SSAN under viewpoint, altitude, spatial-shift, and environmental variations.
author: Fawei Ge, Xinao Wang, Leipo Liu, Huan Wang, Baofeng Ji, Pengju Si

title: Frequency-Interaction Mamba for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
content: Image super-resolution (SR) aims to recover a high-resolution (HR) image from its low-resolution (LR) counterpart, yet accurately reconstructing texture details in complex regions remains challenging. This issue is particularly pronounced in remote sensing images (RSIs), which contain diverse textures and small-scale objects. LR RSIs often suffer from weakened high-frequency (HF) textures and blurred object boundaries, making it difficult to recover both global structures and fine details. Although Transformer-based methods have achieved promising performance, global self-attention usually incurs substantial computational costs. Mamba provides an efficient approach to modeling long-range dependencies, but existing Mamba-based methods remain limited in modeling HF details and 2-D spatial structures. To address these limitations, we propose a frequency-interaction Mamba (FIM) network that jointly enhances long-range dependency modeling, texture reconstruction, and spatial structure representation. Specifically, we design a FIM module (FIMM), in which a frequency enhancement module (FEM) strengthens reconstruction-relevant HF information before state-space modeling and selectively enhances informative texture responses, improving the recovery of edges, textures, and small-scale objects. In addition, we develop a spatial refinement module (SRM), which complements 2-D spatial information through global-guided attention (GGA) and an activation-gated feed-forward network (AGFN), improving the preservation of structural continuity and geometric relationships. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed FIM contains only 15.4M parameters while effectively recovering both global structures and fine-grained details in RSIs.
author: Cuicui Lv, Jiajie Wang, Shuzhen Xu, Wenjie Yan

title: Multiscale Aerosol–Cloud Classification Algorithm of the DQ-1/ACDL
content: Spaceborne LiDAR is a unique tool for profiling clouds and aerosols globally. Following the retirement of the Cloud–Aerosol LiDAR and Infrared Pathfinder Satellite Observations (CALIPSO) mission, DQ-1, carrying the aerosol and carbon dioxide detection LiDAR (ACDL), now fills this observational gap. However, traditional single-profile aerosol–cloud classification algorithms often misclassify overlapping layers and generate “striping artifacts,” characterized by unrealistic horizontal discontinuities between adjacent profiles, which significantly degrade data quality and usability. To address these issues, we propose a multiscale classification algorithm that partitions LiDAR scenes using dynamic windows (ranging from  $1\times 1$  to  $8\times 8$ ) based on signal-to-noise ratio thresholds and classifies layers using particle backscatter coefficients rather than total attenuated backscatter (TAB). This approach effectively reduces striping artifacts and improves aerosol–cloud layer identification, achieving a 74.6% reduction in horizontal discontinuity compared with the cloud–aerosol LiDAR with orthogonal polarization (CALIOP) scene classification algorithm (SCA). Furthermore, comparisons with Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), CALIOP, and the Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2) for dust distribution, cloud-top height (CTH), and cloud phase show general consistency and physically reasonable behavior across diverse regions, supporting the applicability of the ACDL products. The proposed framework ensures the quality of ACDL datasets and offers a transferable approach for optimizing layer classification in other spaceborne LiDAR missions.
author: Luhao Zuo, Feiyue Mao, Weiwei Xu, Lin Zang, Pengfei Hu, Xiuqing Hu, Jiqiao Liu, Wei Gong

title: A Coupled Spatiotemporal Fusion Method for Multisensor Reconstruction
content: Multisensor reconstruction draws on measurements with different physical sensitivities and sampling patterns to estimate a common target. We present a coupled spatiotemporal fusion method that makes these relationships explicit for intermittently sampled event records. The method defines the target response on valid observation opportunities, constructs source records over specified spatial and temporal supports, and combines their representations to estimate a target-record probability. Recorded values and observation availability remain distinct throughout the reconstruction. Matched comparisons determine whether changes in source support, representation, correspondence, or combination add useful capability. An application to the FY-4A lightning mapping imager (LMI) and the International Space Station Lightning Imaging Sensor (ISS-LIS) demonstrates reconstruction in both sensor-role directions and successive contributions from same-cell and neighboring records across six regions. A further implementation jointly uses event records and infrared cloud measurements. On 167 629 targets from 12 dates excluded from development of the recent-cloud operation, recent observations reduce log loss by 10.75% relative to the existing joint-input baseline and increase recall from 46.40% to 61.76% at the same 5% selection fraction. Same-product temporal and same-observation representation comparisons separate the effects of these operations. Evaluation against ground-based cloud-to-ground (CG) records establishes retrieval value beyond direct source counts. The method provides an implemented and testable basis for organizing heterogeneous observations around a common reconstruction task.
author: Nengxing Guo, Li Cai, Biwu Yan, Yingpu Xie, Yongxing Zeng, Chun Zhao, Tao Li, Shanqiang Gu

title: Terrain-Aware Evaluation of Optimized Sparse Source Sampling and Vibroseis Route Planning for Land Seismic Acquisition
content: Land seismic acquisition must balance geophysical sampling quality with field operational cost, yet source-layout design and vibroseis routing are commonly treated separately. We propose a multiobjective workflow that combines sparse source selection with terrain-aware routing evaluation. Sampling quality is screened by the second-peak suppression ratio ( $R_{\mathrm { SPS}}$ ), the normalized off-direct-current (DC) peak sidelobe of the sampling-mask Fourier response. Selected sources are connected using terrain-cost shortest paths and an open traveling salesman problem (TSP) tour. 5-D fast multidimensional singular spectrum analysis (FMSSA) is applied only after selection as an independent reconstruction-validation step. In the main synthetic test at a nominal 20% source sampling rate on the complete candidate grid,  $R_{\mathrm { SPS}}$ -guided simulated annealing ( $R_{\mathrm { SPS}}$ -SA) reduces  $R_{\mathrm { SPS}}$  from 0.714 to 0.287 and route length from 13.51 to 11.48 km relative to constrained-regular sampling; no shortest-route claim is made against every baseline. Thirty random-mask FMSSA tests yield an SNR of  $19.24~\pm ~0.83$  dB and show no clear monotonic relationship between  $R_{\mathrm { SPS}}$  and reconstruction SNR in this benchmark. Under predeclared spectral and coverage constraints, one constraint-satisfying route-focused layout shortens the route by about 19% and lowers terrain cost by about 22% relative to the mean of the 30 random layouts with only a 0.17-dB SNR difference. A central-depot multivehicle extension further shows the trade-off between aggregate travel and maximum per-vehicle workload. The results support the use of  $R_{\mathrm { SPS}}$  as a low-cost preacquisition spectral-risk diagnostic, not a reconstruction-error predictor, and demonstrate that spectral, reconstruction, and operational metrics should be reported together.
author: Yi Guo, Tingquan Deng, Rongzhi Lin, Jianwei Ma

title: SMGNet: A Lightweight Spectral-Mamba-Guided Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image classification faces a fundamental inductive bias conflict: reconciling the physical continuity of spectral sequences with the 2-D topology of spatial structures. Existing methods either disrupt spectral continuity [convolutional neural networks (CNNs)] or destroy spatial topology through forced flattening (Transformers and pure-sequence Mamba models), while conventional dual-branch networks rely on shallow posthoc fusion that overlooks the inherent physical leader–follower relationship between spectral and spatial modalities. To address these challenges, we propose SMGNet, a lightweight spectral-Mamba-guided network that establishes a “spectral leads, spatial follows” paradigm. The spectral branch employs a state space model (Mamba) to efficiently capture global long-range spectral dependencies with linear complexity, while a lightweight Res-CNN preserves intact spatial topology. Central to the framework is the spectral-guided feature modulation module, which transforms global spectral priors into dynamic affine parameters for stagewise conditional injection throughout the spatial network, enabling deep, semantically conditioned cross-modal interaction. Under a rigorous data leakage prevention protocol, SMGNet achieves overall accuracies of 98.88%, 99.07%, and 97.83% on the Pavia University, Salinas, and QUH-Tangdaowan datasets, respectively, with only 0.33 M parameters, demonstrating exceptional accuracy–efficiency tradeoff.
author: Xiaoyang Meng, Longbao Wang, Kaijun Jia, Hongmin Gao

title: RGB Optical Remote Sensing in the Deep Learning Era: A Systematic Review of Methods, Models, Datasets, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
content: The remarkable progress in the areas of computer vision, artificial intelligence, and deep learning (DL), combined with the rapid democratization of unmanned aerial vehicles, has propelled optical remote sensing (ORS) into a central role within the field of Earth observation. Among the available sensing modalities, the visible (red–green–blue, RGB) bands remain the most accessible and widely adopted, as RGB sensors are inexpensive, robust, and produce imagery that is intuitively interpretable without specialized geophysical expertise. The corresponding body of literature is vast and rapidly expanding, spanning diverse tasks, architectures, and methodologies. In this context, the present work provides a systematic and in-depth review of the most recent advances in DL-based RGB ORS, focusing on approaches whose image input at inference time is the RGB bands of satellite, aerial, and drone imagery, whether the visible bands are employed alone, as the primary image input, or as the image branch that is actually instantiated and evaluated within a multimodal system; multiband pretrained backbones are considered only insofar as they are adapted to, and evaluated on, RGB downstream tasks, whereas approaches requiring nonvisible bands at inference are referred to only as context. The review addresses the interpretation of RGB imagery, whereas multiview geometric reconstruction and sensor-level radiometric preprocessing are explicitly delimited as lying outside its scope. Following a structured literature review methodology, the evolution of the field is first delineated through a sequence of distinct research phases and the corresponding milestone works. Subsequently, a multicriteria taxonomy of the literature is formed, examining the addressed tasks, the underlying neural network architectures, the adopted learning strategies, the employed acquisition platforms, the overall design objectives, and the selected application domains; for each criterion, a methodical comparative analysis of the various categories of approaches and critical insights are provided. Moreover, the publicly available RGB ORS datasets are reviewed, accompanied by key observations. Furthermore, a comprehensive and structured discussion of the current challenges and the most promising future research directions in the field is provided.
author: Panagiotis Koletsis, Georgios Angelidis, Vasilis Efthymiou, Dimitrios Michail, Christos N. Chalkias, Thomas Lagkas, Panagiotis Sarigiannidis, Georgios Th. Papadopoulos

title: GNSS-DispFM: A Self-Supervised Foundation Model for Daily GNSS Displacement Time Series
content: Displacement time series from global navigation satellite systems (GNSSs) are essential for a wide range of applications, including monitoring tectonic crustal deformations and investigating the different stages of the earthquake cycle. Machine learning methods have proven promising for GNSS applications; however, most remain fully supervised. This creates a bottleneck as labeled data are scarce, even though large amounts of unlabeled GNSS data are freely available. We present the GNSS displacement foundation model, a self-supervised foundation model for daily GNSS displacement time series. The model uses a dual-stream input combining displacement and velocity-like increments, and is pretrained using a masked latent prediction objective with vector-quantized targets adapted from wav2vec 2.0, with several modifications for geodetic data. Pretrained on data from over 17 000 globally distributed GNSS stations, an analysis of the learned codebook suggests that the representations capture the main signal types in GNSS displacement data, including seismic offsets, tectonic drift, and seasonal patterns. The foundation model is later fine-tuned on two downstream tasks, namely 90-day displacement forecasting and seismic step localization, where it achieves the lowest mean test-set forecasting error, with a clearer advantage in the upper error tail, and substantially improves seismic step localization over the task-specific baselines. These results show that self-supervised pretraining is a promising approach for GNSS displacement time-series analysis.
author: Nick Teutschmann, Laura Crocetti, Fanny Lehmann, Leonardo Trentini, Benedikt Soja

title: DSG-Net: A Dual Semantic Guidance Network for Optical-SAR Image Registration
content: Optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image registration under complex geometric transformations remains a challenging task due to the pronounced discrepancy in imaging mechanisms and noise patterns, as well as the large spatial deformations. Despite recent advancements in sparse keypoint matching and dense correspondence estimation, existing approaches are still dominated by appearance-driven cross-modal similarity, whose stability and discriminability are inherently limited by their intrinsic domain gap. As an attempt to mitigate this problem, we propose DSG-Net, a dual semantic guidance network for optical-SAR image registration which exploits semantic structural information obtained from optical and SAR semantic segmentation, demonstrating enhanced cross-modal robustness against raw intensity representations. Specifically, our method decomposes segmentation maps into complementary semantic edges and semantic interiors, where semantic edges capture modality-invariant geometric structures and furnish robust cross-modal constraints along contours, while semantic interiors offer reliable localization cues under substantial spatial deformations via semantic consistency. Extensive experiments on the WHU-OPT-SAR and DFC2020 datasets show that DSG-Net consistently outperforms sparse and dense registration baselines under various geometric deformation scales. Notably, on the WHU-OPT-SAR dataset our DSG-Net achieves a CMR@1px of 79.40%, yielding a 12.7% relative gain over leading baseline. We further validate the cross-paradigm generalization of our design on both sparse and dense registration framework and achieves noticeable performance gains.
author: Junfang Shi, Zixuan Sun, Jingyuan Xia, La Jiang, Zhen Liu, Shuaifeng Zhi

title: A Deep Learning-Based Approach for Mapping Shrubs in Arctic Tundra From Very High-Resolution Imagery
content: Arctic shrub expansion is accelerating due to climate warming, but accurately mapping it at fine spatial scales remains challenging due to spectral overlap between shrubs and surrounding vegetation, heterogeneous tundra landscapes, and limited availability of very high-resolution imagery. This study presents a novel mapping and validation approach that integrates very high-resolution (<1 m) QuickBird and WorldView satellite imagery across 12 North Slope sites, using deep learning architectures to map changes in shrub cover from 2002 to 2022. Deep learning models, including Convolutional Neural Network, Residual Networks (ResNet), Visual Geometry Group (VGG), U-shaped encoder–decoder network, and Vision Transformer, were trained on 4100 three-channel pansharpened multispectral images (200 × 200 m). Two traditional machine learning models (Random Forest and Support Vector Machine) served as a control group. Leave-one-site-out cross-validation showed that all models performed well (Area Under the Curve - Receiver Operating Characteristic of 0.78–0.86, F1 at validation of 0.33–0.46) and had a moderate to strong agreement with field reference data (R2= 0.76–0.87). The pretrained VGG and ResNet models achieved the strongest field-reference alignments for shrub cover prediction, while the difference with traditional models was small. Temporal trend analyses for July and August demonstrate a cover change of 0.06–0.45% yr−1with unweighted mean area slopes and 0.01–0.92% yr−1inverse-variance weighting. Growth rates were found to depend on the analytical design. Furthermore, the limiting factor in mapping shrub cover was not model complexity but the quality of the training data labels (annotation method explained ∼26% of the error variance). Per-scene cover error was seen across architectures (ρ = 0.67). Comparison with NASA Goddard’s LiDAR, Hyperspectral and Thermal-derived Canopy Height Models revealed a weak-to-moderate relationship (R2= 0.04–0.77), suggesting horizontal cover and vertical canopy structure capture complementary aspects of shrub abundance. These results demonstrate the potential of deep learning to map decadal shrub expansion at submeter resolution.
author: Darko Radakovic, Mark Chopping, Bruce Cook, Aparna S. Varde, Stefan Robila

title: CAS-Mamba: Change-Aware State-Space Modulation in the Encoder for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Most existing Mamba-based remote sensing change detection methods still realize bitemporal interaction mainly at the feature or fusion level, after the initial representations have already been formed. As a result, cross-temporal cues remain only weakly coupled to the state-update mechanism that shapes encoded features. To address this limitation, this article proposes the change-aware state-space modulation framework (CAS-Mamba), which operationalizes cross-temporal interaction during encoding as conditional modulation of two key state-update pathways in a weight-shared Mamba encoder. Specifically, the delta-modulation module injects difference-conditioned signals into the time-step generation pathway to regulate update selectivity according to cross-temporal discrepancy, whereas the B-path modulation module applies context-conditioned gating to regulate the effective write strength of the input injection pathway. In this way, cross-temporal evidence is incorporated into representation formation through pathway-level conditioning rather than through conventional feature-level fusion alone. A lightweight decoder is further introduced to consolidate multiscale change-aware representations and recover spatial details without imposing heavy decoder-side overhead. Experiments on LEVIR-CD+, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD show that CAS-Mamba achieves consistently strong F1-score and intersection over union while maintaining a favorable performance–complexity tradeoff.
author: Shuwen Shen, Kai Xu, Zhiyong Zhang, Yunjiang Cai, Yutao Liu, Wanling Peng

title: TSMRNet: A Method for High-Resolution Soil Moisture Mapping With Limited Labels by Integrating Self-Supervised and Semi-Supervised Learning
content: Soil moisture is critical to terrestrial hydrological cycles, and remote sensing enables high-resolution monitoring. Data-driven approaches are increasingly used for soil moisture mapping, yet scarce in situ measurements and heterogeneous multisource features limit fully supervised models under label-scarce conditions. To address these challenges, we propose the Triple-S moisture retrieval network (TSMRNet), integrating self-supervised and semi-supervised learning for high-resolution soil moisture retrieval. Specifically, multimodal masked feature reconstruction jointly models synthetic aperture radar (SAR), optical, terrain, and soil features through modality-level masking and modality-specific perturbations, enabling cross-modal representation learning from unlabeled data and providing pretrained encoder weights for subsequent semi-supervised learning. The relative wetness classifier reformulates soil moisture estimation as pairwise relative wetness ranking, exploiting unlabeled samples via classification-based semi-supervised learning. In parallel, the forward backscatter reconstruction loss reconstructs SAR backscatter from estimated soil moisture and auxiliary variables, imposing backscatter-consistency constraints on unlabeled predictions. These components are jointly optimized within a unified framework. Using Sentinel-1/2 imagery and auxiliary data, experiments across three observation networks on different continents show that TSMRNet outperforms fully supervised deep learning and ensemble tree models under random-split and station-based split strategies. It remains robust with only 5% labeled samples and demonstrates strong temporal generalization in cross-year validation. Overall, TSMRNet provides an accurate approach to high-resolution soil moisture mapping with limited labels.
author: Mingyang Song, Hong Zhang, Yinhaibin Ding, Yukun Fan, Zhe Wang, Yazhe Xie, Lu Xu, Wenjiang Huang

title: SCAF-Net: Sparse Cross-Modal Adaptive Fusion Network for RGB-IR UAV Object Detection
content: Visible-infrared (RGB-IR) object detection equips uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) with robust, around-the-clock perception capabilities. However, practical deployments are frequently constrained by weak spatial misalignment between heterogeneous sensors. This issue degrades the object detection accuracy of UAVs, for which a modest offset may cause corresponding features to overlap background regions or neighboring instances. In addition, the substantial appearance difference between RGB and infrared imagery makes direct cross-modal matching unreliable. Inspired by feature decoupling paradigms and cross-modal attention mechanisms, we propose a geometry-guided RGB-IR framework termed the sparse cross-modal adaptive fusion network (SCAF-Net) to improve feature correspondence and interaction under such conditions. Specifically, the modality-decoupled offset estimator estimates modality-shared geometric representations and bidirectional offsets. The geometry-aware sparse cross-attention module uses these offsets to perform saliency-guided sparse cross-modal attention with a coordinate-distance bias, while the context-preserving bidirectional warping mechanism reintegrates the enhanced sparse tokens into dense feature maps within the same reference coordinate domain. The key novelty is the unified offset-guided coordinate flow that consistently guides correspondence estimation, token interaction, and feature reconstruction. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle and RGBTDronePerson datasets demonstrate that SCAF-Net achieves competitive performance, exhibiting enhanced robustness in complex aerial-view scenarios.
author: Boyu Zhang, Chaoyang Niu, Wanjie Lu, Wei Liu, Zhen Wang

title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Future Projections of Qinghai Lake Area Changes
content: As the largest inland saline lake on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, Qinghai Lake plays a critical role in regional ecological security. Understanding its surface area dynamics is, therefore, essential for assessing hydroclimatic responses under ongoing climate change. In this study, a seasonal time series of lake area (1987–2021) was reconstructed using long-term Landsat imagery and the normalized multiband water index. By integrating statistical analyses and an ensemble machine learning framework coupled with Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) projections, we investigated the hydroclimatic drivers of lake area variations and projected future lake dynamics. Results show that Qinghai Lake experienced a transition from contraction to rapid expansion around 2004, with rates of $\boldsymbol{-}$3.38 and 9.04 km$^{\boldsymbol{2}}$/year, respectively. Lake area variations were strongly correlated with basin-wide precipitation and Buha River discharge ($\boldsymbol{r = }$ 0.75 and 0.77, respectively), but showed a relatively weak relationship with temperature ($\boldsymbol{r = }$ 0.25). Wavelet coherence analysis further revealed significant correlations at both annual and interannual (2–4 years) scales. Spatial analyses further indicated that the combined effects of precipitation and temperature contributed to shoreline variability. Future projections suggest a noticeable decline in lake area during 2022–2040, followed by fluctuations within a range of approximately 4400–4500 km$^{\boldsymbol{2}}$. This pattern is consistent across shared socioeconomic pathway scenarios and may be associated with relatively stable future precipitation projections under CMIP6. Overall, these findings provide new insights into the spatiotemporal evolution and driving mechanisms of Qinghai Lake and offer a scientific basis for water resource management and climate change adaptation in alpine regions.
author: Futao Wang, Ziqi Zhang, Mingxuan Du, Chao Zeng

title: Decoupling vegetation–soil interactions from hyperspectral reflectance
content:

title: A Fully Passive Second-Order Charge-Domain Noise-Shaping Digital Bang--Bang PLL With Adaptive DCO Gain Controller
content: Quantization noise (QN) is recognized as a primary factor limiting the in-band phase-noise and jitter performance of digital bang–bang phase-locked loops (BBPLLs), while the nonlinear loop gain introduced by the binary phase detector further degrades jitter performance. In order to address these issues, a fully passive second-order noise-shaping BBPLL (NS-BBPLL) with an adaptive digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) gain controller is presented in this article. A fully passive noise-shaping phase detector (NSPD) is employed, by which the phase difference is processed in the charge domain, and second-order shaping of the phase-detector QN is achieved, thereby effectively suppressing its in-band contribution. As a result, a measured 6-dB in-band phase-noise improvement is achieved through the combined reduction of the detector quantization- and thermal-noise (TN) contributions, with the larger reduction observed in the QN term. In addition, an adaptive DCO gain controller based on a symbolic least-mean-squares (LMSs) algorithm is introduced to automatically optimize the loop bandwidth and improve the overall jitter performance. The proposed integer- $N$  NS-BBPLL is fabricated in a 65-nm process, with a core area of 0.12 mm2. The core circuit’s power consumption is 2.50 mW at an output frequency of 4.8 GHz. Jitter of 305 fsrms is achieved, and the reference spur is measured at −59 dBc, resulting in a figure of merit (FoM) of −246.3 dB.
author: Zijing Yuan, Yu Xin, Qianshui Yu, Peiyuan Wan, Xu Liu, Wei Deng, Zhijie Chen

title: SPACE: Safety-Critical Performance-Counter Adaptive Control Engine for Anomaly Mitigation via Deep Reinforcement Learning
content: Modern automotive systems require adaptive mechanisms to handle both accidental faults and security threats at runtime. While hardware performance counter (HPC)-based anomaly detection has shown promise in RISC-V platforms, detection alone is insufficient; identifying anomalies without an effective response cannot prevent system failures or security breaches. In safety-critical environments, timely mitigation is essential to preserve system reliability and safety. To bridge this gap, this article proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based anomaly mitigation approach that learns adaptive recovery policies from HPC observations, building on prior HPC-based anomaly detection for RISC-V platforms. The problem is formulated as a Markov decision process (MDP) where the DRL agent selects among three recovery actions: advance, restart, or backtrack. The DRL agent is trained on benchmarks running in FreeRTOS with injected faults and subsequently deployed as the safety-critical performance-counter adaptive control engine (SPACE). To satisfy hard real-time constraints, SPACE implements the trained DRL agent on a dedicated SiLago dynamically reconfigurable resource array (DRRA) fabric. Compared to software-based execution on general-purpose RISC-V processors, which severely violates system deadlines, the hardware-accelerated SPACE framework achieves strictly deterministic inference that is over three orders of magnitude faster. Furthermore, it provides critical physical and temporal isolation from the main CPU workloads while maintaining a minimal silicon footprint up to  $17\times $  smaller than high-performance out-of-order (O3) cores.
author: Elio Vinciguerra, Nooshin Nosrati, Giuseppe Ascia, Maurizio Palesi, Ahmed Hemani

title: LUT-DiT: A LUT-Based Diffusion Transformer Accelerator for Scalable LUT Inference
content: Large-scale diffusion transformers (DiTs) (e.g., FLUX.1) deliver strong generation quality but face severe memory and latency bottlenecks. Although lookup table (LUT)-based inference eliminates expensive multiplications, conventional LUT schemes that precompute all weight-activation combinations suffer from prohibitive table growth, resulting in 178.81 GB of precomputed tables for FLUX.1 under W4A4 quantization. To address this problem, this article proposes LUT-DiT, a LUT-based DiT accelerator for scalable LUT inference. First, we employ outlier-aware product quantization (PQ) to map weights into a compact codebook domain, thereby shifting precomputation from the full weight domain to the codebook domain. Second, we introduce a two-level lookup mechanism that reformulates full weight-activation precomputation as index-to-codebook mapping followed by codebook-activation lookup, reducing memory complexity from  $O(N_{\text {weight}}{\,}\times {\,}2^{b_{\text {act}}})$  to  $O(N_{\text {codebook}}{\,}\times {\,}2^{b_{\text {act}}})$ . Third, we design a pipelined datapath with input-channel (IC) sharing and symmetry-based compression, reducing the active on-chip working set of precomputed tables to 2.75 KB. This compact working set is efficiently managed by a three-level on-chip storage hierarchy. Experimental results on FLUX.1 show that LUT-DiT reduces the global off-chip storage required by precomputed tables from 178.81 to 5.124 GB, achieving a  $34.9\times $  reduction, while delivering  $3.15\times $  higher throughput (steps/s) and  $6.76\times $  higher energy efficiency than an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. Compared with the gains reported by Diff-DiT over its GPU baseline, the corresponding ratios of reported gains are  $2.26\times $  and  $1.21\times $  for throughput and energy efficiency, respectively.
author: Enhao Tang, Yongyang Yin, Wei Li, Faxun Jin, Zhongfeng Wang, Jun Lin

title: SATurbine: A Multicore Transformer Accelerator With Gated Broadcast for Efficient Dynamic Sparse Attention
content: Transformer models have shown outstanding performance in natural language processing and computer vision. However, their attention mechanism incurs substantial computation and memory overhead that grows rapidly with sequence length. Although studies have shown that attention distributions are often sparse, dynamically exploiting this sparsity remains an enormous challenge due to the limitations coming from accurately identifying important interactions and handling inefficient hardware behavior caused by zero-value operations and irregular memory accesses. To resolve these issues, this work presents SATurbine, a software–hardware codesigned accelerator for dynamic sparse attention. At the algorithm level, SATurbine introduces a hardware-friendly sparsity prediction method that combines interval-based quantization with Top-K selection to identify and eliminate redundant attention links. Evaluations on the long-range arena (LRA) benchmark demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive accuracy across five tasks while pruning up to 95% of attention connections. At the hardware level, SATurbine integrates a dedicated prediction unit and a sparse-attention computation engine to support operator fusion and data reuse, thereby reducing the overhead of zero-value computations. Moreover, a multicore architecture with a gated broadcasting mechanism is employed to improve token-level parallelism and limit irregular sparse memory accesses. Simulation and synthesis results demonstrate that SATurbine achieves speedups of  $3.84\times $ ,  $2.36\times $ , and  $1.61\times $  compared with A3, SpAtten, and Sanger, respectively. Relative to general-purpose computing platforms, average speedups of  $7.01\times $  over an Intel Core i5-14600KF CPU and  $2.64\times $  over an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU are achieved.
author: Wentao Xu, Yuxuan Zhang, Rongzhou Zhu, Xiang Wu, Zehao Wang, Weilin Li, Jiaxiang Wang, Chunyang Du, Yuanlu Gao, Zhanxiang Gao, Fengdong Qu, Jinming Lu, Li Du

title: Scalable AXI4 Transaction Monitoring for Mixed-Criticality SoCs: From Phase-Level Precision to ID-Level Efficiency
content: Mixed-criticality systems-on-chip (SoCs) with on-chip interconnects based on the Advanced eXtensible Interface 4 (AXI4) open standard protocol lack a protocol-level timeout mechanism, exposing systems to deadlocks and missed real-time deadlines when subordinate devices or managers fail or stall due to hardware faults, radiation-induced upsets, or software errors. This work presents a configurable hardware intellectual property (IP), nonintrusive in fault-free operation, that detects AXI4 protocol violations and timing faults at runtime and restores interconnect liveness through a cut-and-drain isolation mechanism. To address the fundamental tradeoff between monitoring granularity and area cost, we introduce three designs at decreasing monitoring granularity: phase-level tracking (PLT), which provides cycle-accurate fault localization across individual protocol phases; channel-level tracking (CLT), which coalesces per-phase monitors into channel-level supervision; and ID-level tracking (ILT), which achieves sublinear area scaling by monitoring only per-ID transaction boundaries. Synthesized in GlobalFoundries 12-nm technology, CLT reduces area by 36.7% relative to PLT while preserving worst case detection bounds at a minimal detection latency overhead, whereas ILT achieves an 89.2% area reduction suitable for tightly constrained deployments at the cost of a  $3.7\times $  higher median detection latency with coarser fault localization. Fault injection campaigns on a RISC-V SoC across 1.2 million scenarios confirm that no fault manifesting as an AXI4 protocol or liveness violation escaped detection, with observed detection latencies consistently bounded by theoretical worst case predictions.
author: Chaoqun Liang, Thomas Benz, Alessandro Ottaviano, Michael Rogenmoser, Luca Benini, Angelo Garofalo, Davide Rossi

title: A Posit-FP-Mixed FMA With Bitwidth-Adaptive Clocking and Accuracy-Throughput Optimization
content: The Posit number system has been introduced to enhance the decimal accuracy for values with small exponents by adopting a nonuniform dynamic range and precision, as opposed to the conventional IEEE-754 floating-point (FP) number system that imposes uniform accuracy across a wide range of exponents. However, conventional FP-only or Posit-only number systems exhibit computational inefficiencies and accuracy constraints: 1) dynamic timing slack (DTS) arising from unused mantissa bits remains unexploited; 2) accuracy is affected by the range of data magnitudes. In this work, we propose: 1) a run-time bitwidth-based adaptive clocking for throughput improvement by exploiting the DTS based on run-time mantissa bitwidth; 2) a mixed Posit-FP number system supporting additional accuracy-oriented and performance-oriented mixed data formats. Measurement results on a 40-nm test chip show that up to 79.6% throughput improvement is achieved by the proposed bitwidth-based adaptive clocking scheme at only 2.2% area overhead. Additionally, the mixed Posit-FP number system can maintain either the highest throughput or the highest accuracy across a wide numerical magnitude range of  $10^{-30}\sim 10^{30}$ .
author: Ruijie Peng, Humiao Li, Zhen Kong, Jin Wang, Weirong Dong, Yida Li, Jiamin Li, Longyang Lin

title: A 9.75-Gb/s Matrix-Assisted Anchor-Decoding TPC Decoder for NAND Flash Memories
content: With the increasing storage demand driven by artificial intelligence and other data-intensive applications, nand flash memories require error-correction code (ECC) solutions that provide sufficient correction capability while maintaining low power consumption. Although low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoders are widely used in modern nand flash controllers, their soft-decision decoding process usually introduces high implementation complexity and power overhead. Turbo product codes (TPCs), which rely on iterative hard-decision decoding (iHDD), offer a low-complexity alternative. In this work, a matrix-assisted anchor-decoding (MA-AD) TPC decoder architecture is proposed. The proposed design employs an error matrix, conflict registers, and a rollback handling unit to realize conflict detection and rollback operations. By reorganizing the dynamic and irregular anchor-decoding procedure into a static matrix-assisted decoding flow, the proposed architecture becomes more suitable for hardware implementation. Compared with the conventional extended Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (eBCH)-based TPC decoder, the proposed MA-AD TPC decoder improves the correction capability in the waterfall region by 0.25 dB with a limited reduction in throughput. Implementation results show that the proposed decoder achieves an area of 0.49 mm2, a throughput of 9.75 Gb/s, and an energy efficiency of 6.5 pJ/bit.
author: Wenyi Yang, Jianjun Luo, Yifan Shen, Cankun Huang, Tianwei Gui, Ying He, Jiaxin Xu

title: An NRZ/PAM-4 Dual-Mode Transmitter Using Tx-Interleaving Technique for Low-Power DRAM Interfaces
content: This article proposes a nonreturn-to-zero (NRZ)/PAM-4 dual-mode transmitter for low-power double data rate (LPDDR) memory interfaces that employs a transmitter-interleaving (TI) technique to enhance power efficiency while maintaining high-speed signaling capability. Instead of separate data and clock paths in the conventional dual-mode transmitters, the proposed architecture inserts clock-controlled NMOS switches into the low-voltage swing-terminated logic (LVSTL) output driver structure, thereby merging the serialization path with the driver stage. This structural integration eliminates the need for a dedicated high-speed serializer and reduces switching activity in the driver block. A prior TI driver-based transmitter requires a clock bootstrapping circuit and typically does not support ZQ calibration, resulting in impedance mismatch. In contrast, this work removes the bootstrapping circuit and adopts a dual-mode ZQ calibration scheme that maintains constant output impedance across both NRZ and PAM-4 modes. A prototype chip is fabricated in a 1-poly 10-metal (1P10LM) 28-nm CMOS process. Measured results demonstrate that the proposed transmitter consumes 10.82 mW while transmitting 11-Gb/s PAM-4 data, achieving an energy efficiency of 0.98-pJ/b, confirming that the proposed structure is highly suitable for LPDDR.
author: Hang-Min Jo, Young-Min Lee, Jun-Sung Kim, Won-Young Lee

title: Leak-CIM: A PVT-Robust and Energy-Efficient SRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro Exploiting Transistor Leakage
content: The binarized neural networks (BNNs) significantly reduce arithmetic and storage costs for edge inference, but repeated bitwise accumulation and memory access still limit system energy efficiency. This article presents leak-computing-in-memory (CIM), a  $256\times 64$  static random access memory (SRAM)-based voltage-mode CIM macro that exploits the subthreshold leakage of off-state transistors as ultrahigh-impedance pseudo-resistors for low-energy analog accumulation. Unlike charge-sharing CIMs, the proposed scheme maintains a wide read-bitline (RBL) dynamic range while strongly suppressing the shoot-through current that typically limits voltage-mode operation. To compensate for the process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensitivity of leakage-based pull-up and pull-down paths, the leak-CIM employs a postfabrication N-well bias calibration scheme that restores their resistance balance. The postlayout simulations show that the calibrated macro maintains a normalized mean-squared error below  $1.12\times 10^{-2}$  across 40 global PVT conditions. Fabricated in a 22-nm bulk-CMOS process, the macro achieves up to 1799 TOPS/W and 31.67 TOPS/mm2 across measured operating points. When the measured ADC characteristics are incorporated into a BNN inference model, leak-CIM attains 98.15% accuracy on MNIST and 86.04% on CIFAR-10.
author: Hiroto Tagata, Takashi Sato, Hiromitsu Awano

title: A 28-nm Floating-Point SRAM-CIM Macro With In-Array Shifting for Exponent Normalization and Mantissa Alignment Based on Exponent Midrange
content: Floating-point computing-in-memory (FP-CIM) macros typically suffer from prohibitive area and power overheads due to the complexity of alignment logic. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel FP-CIM macro that integrates two key in-memory operations: shifting-in-memory exponent normalization (SIMENP) and shifting-in-memory mantissa alignment (SIMMAP). SIMENP enables in-array exponent shifting using the proposed 9T bitcell, thereby eliminating redundant processing latency. For mantissa alignment, a midrange-based subtraction-shifting scheme is implemented using the proposed 10T bitcell, which obviates the need for dedicated shift registers while halving the clock cycles required for data shifting. The proposed macro is designed and simulated in a 28-nm CMOS process with a 36-kB capacity. Simulation results demonstrate an energy efficiency of 11.63 TFLOPS/W at 150 MHz under a 0.55 V supply. Compared to state-of-the-art subtractor-based FP-CIM architectures and D flip-flop (DFF) combined schemes, the proposed design reduces the shifting-logic area by 45.7%, while also reducing the number of cycles required for mantissa alignment by 50%.
author: Qiang Zhao, Fugui Jiang, Yang Yang, Juntao Ge, Miao Long, Chenglong Duan, Zhiting Lin

title: Pipelined Microarchitecture for VTA With Circuit and Instruction Co-Optimization
content: Tensor virtual machine–versatile tensor accelerator (TVM–VTA) stack is an end-to-end deep neural network (DNN) accelerator template known for its high reconfigurability and flexibility. However, baseline TVM–VTA accelerator templates may introduce pipeline and scheduling inefficiencies. Pipelined VTA (PVTA) focuses on the specific execution bottlenecks of the TVM–VTA stack and develops a pipeline-oriented solution across microarchitecture and instruction flow. The proposed architecture redesigns the GEMM and ALU pipelines, instruction flow, LOAD module, and dual-thread dependency mechanism, while maintaining compatibility with the existing software-hardware stack. Implemented on Xilinx ZCU104 FPGA, the proposed PVTA achieves a DSP efficiency of 0.564, delivering  $3.9\times $  and  $2.54\times $  speedups over the original VTA on ResNet-50 and YOLOv3, with final throughputs of 29.2 and 7.25 fps, respectively. These improvements demonstrate the effectiveness of pipeline-focused optimizations in enhancing VTA’s performance for end-to-end DNN acceleration. Evaluation against representative VTA-based designs shows that PVTA attains the highest reported end-to-end speedup within the VTA framework. Compared to other leading architectures, the proposed approach achieves comparable or higher performance while preserving a high degree of flexibility, enabling VTA to evolve from a research template into a competitive, high-performance end-to-end accelerator.
author: Xuhui Wang, Chenglong Zeng, Yinghai Zhao, Yanshuo Gao, Guohe Zhang, Jizhong Zhao, Kuizhi Mei

title: Instruction-Driven Dynamically Reconfigurable Lockstep Architecture for Runtime Reliability
content: Advanced process scaling has introduced significant reliability challenges where microprocessors exhibit highly dynamic sensitivity to transient faults across varying operating environments and application phases. Conventional static lockstep architectures impose rigid redundancy levels, leading to either permanent resource wastage or an inflexible reliability boundary. This article presents an instruction-driven dynamically reconfigurable lockstep architecture that provides a continuum of capabilities for requirement-defined redundancy. Leveraging custom RISC-V instruction set architecture (ISA) extensions, software modulates hardware resources across six operational modes, ranging from high-performance symmetric independent execution to high-reliability triple-core lockstep (TCLS). This reconfiguration is managed by a lockstep controller and an access switching unit (ASU) matrix, achieving mode transitions within a deterministic window of 3–10 cycles. Implemented on 28-nm CMOS, the triple-core CV32E40P cluster achieves 617 MHz. Compared to a standalone baseline core, the architecture occupies  $3.18\times $  area and consumes  $2.64\times $  power, with a marginal frequency penalty of 4.94%. Fault injection campaigns confirm a bounded recovery latency of less than 115 cycles across all redundancy modes. This framework enables software-defined alignment of hardware reliability with runtime requirements.
author: Haijin Zhang, Yuanyuan Cui, Qingbo Yang, Jiangtao Wang, Xunying Zhang

title: DSRVC-DP: A High-Performance Domain-Specific Controller With Memoized CORDIC Extension of RISC-V for Digital Power Applications
content: Digital power control applications impose stringent real-time computational demands, particularly for trigonometric operations in closed-loop systems. To address this challenge, we propose a domain-specific RISC-V controller for digital power (DSRVC-DP), a customized controller based on the tinyriscv open-source processor. The design extends the RISC-V instruction set with hardware-accelerated trigonometric operations via a memoized CORDIC unit, which exploits data reuse to eliminate redundant iterations. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements over DSP and ARM controllers. Single-angle evaluation and trigonometric-table generation are significantly accelerated, and the interrupt service routine (ISR) execution time in closed-loop control is reduced by 48% and 27% in inverter control, and by 36% and 11% in the phase-locked-loop (PLL) applications, respectively. These results confirm DSRVC-DP’s effectiveness in enhancing real-time performance for digital power control.
author: Shijie Chen, Wei Chen, Baoyi Wang, Zhengchun Liu, Jiafeng Ding

title: TREA: Low-Precision Time-Multiplexed, Resource-Efficient Edge Accelerator for Object Detection and Classification
content: This work presents TREA, a low-precision, time-multiplexed, and resource-efficient edge-AI accelerator for object detection and classification, targeting the stringent area-power-latency constraints of edge vision platforms. The proposed architecture integrates a dual-precision (4-/8-bit) quantized SIMD MAC (DQ-MAC) unit based on most-significant-digit-first (MSDF) shift-and-add computation with runtime bit truncation, eliminating conventional multiplier overhead and reducing the accumulator bit width. The DQ-multiply-accumulate (MAC) supports  $4\times $  F  $\times $  P4 or  $1\times $  F  $\times $  P8 operations per cycle, achieving up to  $4\times $  throughput improvement without hardware duplication. A structured hardware-aware reductive pruning (SHARP) strategy is co-designed with the single instruction multiple data (SIMD) datapath, enabling near 50% structured sparsity while maintaining full MAC utilization. This allows a  $3 \times 3$  convolution kernel to be computed in 1 cycle in F  $\times $  P4 mode, compared to 9 cycles in F  $\times $  P8, and a  $5 \times 5$  kernel in 3 cycles, versus 25 cycles, yielding up to a  $9\times $  latency reduction at the kernel level. The accelerator further incorporates a shared reconfigurable quantise-enabled CORDIC-based nonlinear activation function (RQ-NAF) core with a nine-stage pipeline, supporting Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU at one output per cycle after pipeline fill, while enabling (N-1) hardware reuse through time-multiplexing. The complete TREA architecture employs a 1-D array of 128 SIMD DQ-MAC units with layerwise hardware reuse, significantly reducing area and control complexity. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in latency, hardware utilization, and energy efficiency compared to conventional fixed-precision and nonreconfigurable accelerators, validating TREA as an effective solution for real-time edge vision workloads.
author: Vijay Pratap Sharma, Mukul Lokhande, Ratko Pilipović, Omkar Kokane, Santosh Kumar Vishvakarma

title: Design of RF PAs With Pixelated Structure Assisted by Binary PSO Algorithm
content: A gradual evolution can be seen in the design methods for radio frequency (RF) power amplifiers (PAs) as artificial intelligence (AI) technology advances. Traditional design methods that rely on specific structures are being steadily improved by new approaches. In combination with intelligent technology, irregular structures have been used in the design of PAs to provide greater flexibility. A new general design method for RF PAs is presented in this article involving the combination of a pixelated microstrip structure and an improved binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) method. By pixelating the microstrip lines into discrete regions represented by a 0–1 matrix, the matching network (MN) is made more flexible and efficient. In the initial attempt, the predetermined step-type matching circuit of the existing 0.5–4.5 GHz PA was pixelated in order to increase drain efficiency (DE) from 48% to over 55.8%. With a single pixelated microstrip line of 10   $\times $  5 mm, an MN of the PA with a bandwidth of 2–3 GHz was designed without any predetermined topology. To extend the bandwidth, the input microstrip line was increased to 20   $\times $  5 mm, and a 1.5–3.5 GHz single-ended PA was successfully designed, providing an output power greater than 40 dBm and efficiency over 60%. This methodology was subsequently applied to design a sequential load-modulated balanced amplifier (SLMBA), with a saturated output power of 42.7–43.18 dBm, an efficiency of 71.1%–72.13%, and a 10-dB back-off efficiency between 50.4% and 54.1%. In addition, all of the fabricated PAs undergo a modulated signal test using a 20-MHz 5G new radio signal, and excellent linearity is obtained after digital predistortion (DPD).
author: Yunguang Hong, Maojia Geng, Zhiming Fan, Jialin Cai

title: A 3.22-pJ/bit, 3.5-MF2 Modeling-Attack-Resilient Lightweight Strong PUF Based on Add-Rotate-XOR
content: Strong physically unclonable functions (PUFs) provide an exponentially large challenge–response pair (CRP) space for authentication. However, conventional single-bit-response designs must be evaluated repeatedly to assemble a protocol-sized response, increasing communication, latency, and energy overhead. Supporting wider responses reduces this evaluation burden but often involves elaborate transformation logic and substantial area overhead. This article presents a lightweight strong PUF architecture that supports 128-bit CRPs, aligning with standard cryptographic hardware interfaces. By leveraging add-rotate-xor (ARX)-based iterative mixing, the proposed PUF combines modular addition with carry propagation, bit rotations, and roundwise xor-based diffusion and entropy injection to achieve high diffusion, strong nonlinearity, and area efficiency. Implemented in a 180-nm CMOS process, the fabricated prototype occupies an area of 3.5 MF2, achieves a measured throughput of 202 Mbps at 0.8 V within the reliability-characterized operating range, consumes as little as 3.22 pJ/bit, and exhibits a bit error rate (BER) below 5E-7. Statistical evaluations, including the NIST SP 800-22 test suite, the NIST SP 800-90B evaluation, and additional analyses, confirm high randomness and low interbit correlation across the 128-bit responses, even under correlated Gray code challenges. Modeling attacks trained on 40 million CRPs show that the prediction accuracy is close to random guessing, reflecting the high nonlinearity of the challenge–response mapping and its resistance to the evaluated machine learning attacks. These results indicate that the proposed PUF provides an efficient and secure authentication solution for resource-constrained IoT systems.
author: Zhenzhe Chen, Kunyang Liu, Weirong Dong, Takashi Sato

title: Unifying Feed-Forward and Weight-Gradient: An Energy-Efficient Architecture for On-Chip SNN Learning
content: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) enable efficient on-chip learning but face a critical hardware challenge due to the computational asymmetry between small-kernel convolution operations in the feed-forward (FF) stage and large-kernel ones in the weight-gradient (WG) stage. Directly mapping these conflicting patterns onto a static architecture disrupts data locality, typically necessitating either disjoint processing units or redundant data movement, which severely compromises energy efficiency. This brief presents an architecture for unified learning in SNN (AULiS), a sparsity-aware accelerator supporting low-cost BFloat16 local learning (LL) via reconfigurable engines. Its core innovation is an algorithm-architecture codesign. We reformulate the WG stage into broadcast multiplications and map it to an output-stationary (OS) dataflow, newly applied to WG, complementing the weight-stationary (WS) dataflow used for FF. This strategy matches the distinct data-reuse characteristics of each stage: locking weights during FF and weight gradients during WG, allowing a single reconfigurable engine to process both, thereby minimizing data access and maximizing compute density and energy efficiency. Implemented in a 28-nm process, AULiS occupies 2.24 mm2 and achieves this unification with only a 3.4% area overhead. The architecture reaches 23.0 TFLOPS/W in inference and 22.3 TFLOPS/W in training, in dense-equivalent FLOPs at 95% zero sparsity. In a fair comparison, this represents a  $3.78\times $  training and  $1.50\times $  inference improvement in normalized energy efficiency over prior SOTA while delivering up to  $10.64\times $  higher normalized compute density. The high and balanced efficiencies prove that learning can be unified with high-performance inference without efficiency compromise for adaptive edge artificial intelligence (AI).
author: Yue Zuo, Ning Ning, Zhiao Su, Zhilin Li, Shengxin Wang, Chengwang Wu, Zhiwei You, Guanchao Qiao, Yang Liu, Shaogang Hu

title: SHAP: A Sparsity-Aware Hierarchical-Topology-Driven Ising Annealing Processor for Boolean Satisfiability Problems
content: Boolean satisfiability (SAT) stands as a fundamental problem that underpins a wide spectrum of electronic design automation (EDA) and artificial intelligence (AI) tasks. While the Ising model provides a powerful alternative for SAT solving, existing Ising-based solvers suffer from excessive storage overhead and complex mapping topologies. This brief presents a novel sparsity-aware hierarchical-topology-driven Ising annealing processor (SHAP) to address these challenges for 3-SAT problems. Benefiting from the proposed hierarchical Ising topology and its customized simulated annealing (SA) algorithm, the solving process is efficiently accelerated. Furthermore, by utilizing the hybrid coefficient management strategy, the memory overhead is significantly reduced. The proposed processor is simulated with a postlayout netlist in a 28-nm CMOS technology with an operating frequency of 200 MHz. The proposed design is validated using the SATLIB and self-generated dataset, with problem sizes of up to 50 variables and 218 clauses. It achieves a 97% solvability rate for 30–126 instances. While the benchmark MiniSat guarantees 100% solvability, our design delivers a  $5\times $  speedup on successfully solved trials.
author: Junyi Mai, Zhanhong Huang, Longyuan Kang, Chunyao Ruan, Zhihong Cheng, Enyi Yao

title: Glitch-Power Optimization Based on Effective Glitch-Source Identification and Holistic Glitch-Power Attribution
content: With technology scaling and design complexity increasing, glitch-induced dissipation has become nonnegligible in the dynamic power of digital circuits. In ASIC designs, glitch optimization is commonly realized through gate-level or netlist-level structural refinements, whose ability to achieve substantial power reduction with minimal circuit modifications depends on accurately identifying critical cells with high glitch-power impact. However, existing analysis methods misdirect optimization toward less-critical cells, because effective glitch-generation sources are not distinguished and glitch-induced power contribution is incompletely assessed. To address these limitations, this brief proposes a simulation-based glitch analysis and optimization framework. First, a waveform-analysis-based glitch classification algorithm rigorously distinguishes intrinsic glitch generation from propagation, resolving glitch-source misidentification. Then, the holistic glitch-power contribution (HGPC) attribution framework decomposes aggregate glitch-induced power and attributes both self-consumed and downstream propagation-induced components to effective sources, explicitly incorporating glitch-induced internal power ignored by conventional methods. Finally, a signoff-verified greedy engineering change order (ECO) gate downsizing framework validates the proposed analysis method in postlayout optimization. Experiments on several glitch-intensive benchmark circuits using 22-nm CMOS technology demonstrate average reductions of 32.9% in glitch power and 17.2% in total power, with only 11.08% of cells modified, significantly outperforming existing simulation-based methods.
author: Ridong Huang, Qiang Li, Shushan Qiao

title: 28-nm High-Consistency SRAM-CIM Macro With Cascode Current Mirror for Convolutional Neural Networks
content: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), neural network applications demand increasingly efficient data processing. The traditional von Neumann architecture faces a growing “memory wall” bottleneck, making computing-in-memory (CIM) a highly promising solution. This brief presents a 4-Kb 10T static random access memory (SRAM)-CIM macro designed for convolutional neural networks (CNNs), featuring a charge–discharge consistency circuit based on a cascode current mirror that provides stable bias voltages for current-domain computation. The proposed architecture significantly improves the consistency and linearity of bitline charging and discharging, thereby enhancing computational accuracy. Furthermore, only four tail transistors in the 10T SRAM bit cell are used to perform computation, greatly improving throughput. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the SRAM-CIM macroachieves an energy efficiency of 26.43–68.78 TOPS/W and a throughput of 1016 GOPS. With four-bit signed input and four-bit unsigned weight precision, the circuit achieves estimated inference accuracies of 93.4% on the MNIST dataset and 81.6% on the CIFAR-10 dataset.
author: Yaohua Xu, Zhenhao Zuo, Shengyuan Yan, Zhihao Li, Xiaobo Gong, Shijie Xu, Qiangqiang Lu, Xiulong Wu, Chunyu Peng

title: High-Throughput and Area-Efficient Parallel Multimode BCH Encoder
content: This brief proposes a high-throughput, area-efficient parallel multimode Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (BCH) encoder. The conventional multimode architecture relies on multiplexed feedback loops that create severe timing bottlenecks and hinder logic optimization in parallel implementations. The proposed encoder replaces the feedback multiplexer with a fixed feedback path by employing an AND-gate-based control method, enabling a unified matrix formulation and common subexpression elimination (CSE) across all error-correction modes. Synthesis results in 28-nm CMOS demonstrate up to 52% area reduction and up to 78% critical path delay reduction, resulting in higher achievable throughput under the same parallelization setting, compared to the conventional encoding architecture.
author: Hansol Jeong, Jeongmin Kim, Jaehoon Kwon, In-Cheol Park

title: A Low-Bit-First Multiprecision Processing Element for Energy-Efficient FPGA Implementation
content: Multiprecision multiply-accumulate (MAC) units from INT2 to FP32 are increasingly needed on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). However, the existing processing element (PE) designs mostly follow application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC)-oriented composition strategies. Their alignment and selection networks map to lookup table (LUT)-based multiplexing logic and incur rapidly increasing delay on FPGA platforms. We perform a controlled study of composition depth on three Xilinx platforms, spanning the Zynq-7000, Kintex UltraScale+, and Zynq UltraScale+ families. Each added composition layer incurs a steady frequency penalty, and four or more layers lose roughly half of the full-width maximum frequency. Based on this result, we propose hybrid high-precision composition (HHPC). The HHPC bounds in-array composition to a fixed depth. It moves residual high-precision assembly to postarray logic or inter-PE cooperation. It also preserves a fixed control structure across all modes. Based on HHPC, we implement a reconfigurable PE that supports INT2, INT4, INT8, FP16, and FP32 in a unified pipeline. FP32 is supported in two modes. A single PE produces one result every three cycles. A cooperative 3-PE tile sustains one FP32 MAC per cycle. On ZCU102, the proposed design achieves up to 310.60 GOPS/W for INT2 and 3.24 GFLOPS/W for FP32. It delivers up to  $3.0\times $  higher energy efficiency than a comparable reconfigurable multiprecision PE with the same precision coverage.
author: Haotian Liu, Xicheng Lu, Ke Li, Yujie Ma, Kaiyuan Yang, Tiantai Deng, Xiaoyu Yu

title: A Low-Power Unified Swish and GELU Activation Accelerator for CNNs and Transformers
content: Nonlinear activation functions, particularly Swish and Gaussian error linear unit (GELU), have become integral components of modern convolutional neural network (CNN) and Transformer architectures. This work presents low-power unified non-linear activation (LUNA), a high-accuracy LUNA accelerator that efficiently supports both Swish and GELU activations using a unified datapath, and a piecewise-linear approximation based on the first-order derivatives of the activation functions, achieving high accuracy with low power consumption. Implemented in a TSMC 28-nm technology, LUNA achieves up to 80% and 96% reductions in area and power, respectively, with negligible approximation error at the activation-function level compared to prior state-of-the-art designs. Extensive evaluations on CNN models (LeNet-5, EfficientNet-B0, and YOLOv5) and a Transformer model (ViT-B/16) demonstrate that the proposed approximations preserve, and in several cases slightly improve, network-level inference accuracy relative to using an exact fixed-point (FXP) implementation. These results highlight the practicality and scalability of LUNA for next-generation deep-learning hardware.
author: Pragun Jaswal, B. Srinivasu

title: An Energy-Efficient, Low-Complexity Parallel Stochastic Multiplier Using Partial Products
content: Stochastic computing (SC) is widely used in image processing due to its low hardware cost. However, it suffers from high latency caused by long bit streams. Although many parallel stochastic multipliers have been proposed, they are often complex. This work proposes an energy-efficient, low-complexity parallel stochastic multiplier (ELPSM). The ELPSM performs and operations based on uniform allocation, achieving high precision. The resulting outputs correspond to the summation of binary partial products (PPs) through shifting and concatenation. A unified formula is presented to design the ELPSM for arbitrary bit widths based on these PPs. Furthermore, approximate parallel counters (APCs) are utilized to optimize the ELPSM. Both the ELPSM and its optimized variants are formulated for easy scalability to higher bit widths. After optimization, the proposed multiplier reduces delay, power-delay product (PDP), and area-delay product (ADP) by 29.16%, 51.27%, and 50.78%, respectively, compared to a 32-bit binary multiplier, while achieving improvements of 18.81%, 32.33%, and 27.65% over the state-of-the-art 32-bit designs, respectively. The design demonstrates excellent performance in image multiplication and neural network inference; even the APC-optimized variants incur at most 0.45% accuracy loss on benchmark models such as ResNet-18 without posttraining.
author: Yudi Zhao, Qiang He, Zhihuai Zhang, Xiaofei Nie, Ye Lu, Shisheng Xiong, Kai Zhao
